text:
kai: Heads-up — alert from auth-mon: sudden spike in SSO session revokes + MFA push failures for multiple orgs in eu-west-1. Not classic impossible-travel, looks like burst from rotating IPs hitting the same service client IDs. sample alert: `authmon: tenant=acme-corp event=push_fail count=312 window=5m client_id=svc-legacy-5`

sec-bot: :rotating_light: automated detection: high MFA push failure rate (threshold exceeded) for client_id=svc-legacy-5. Incident ticket created #INC-2026-842

alyssa: do we have any user-facing lockouts yet? are users reporting being spammed by pushes?

matt: ops dashboard showing elevated 2FA rejects and token refresh failures. No mass password-reset requests yet but ~60 account lockouts in last 10m. IPs look like a small rotating pool, ASN looks suspicious (proxy hosters).

jess: can we soft-contain? suggestions:
- throttle pushes for that client_id
- revoke refresh tokens for sessions created in last 24h for that client
- add IP ranges to temporary blocklist
Also can infra check if a recent RBAC or KMS change could've caused mis-signed tokens causing retries?

kai: good call. I don't think it's KMS; no key rotation events in the last 48h per kms-audit. But let's verify. @ops-oncall can you run quick token-revoke for svc-legacy-5 and add throttle rule?

ops-oncall: running now. Command I used:
```
# revoke refresh tokens for client
curl -X POST -H "Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN_TOKEN" \
  https://auth.redwood.example.internal/admin/revoke_tokens \
  -d '{"client_id":"svc-legacy-5","age_lt_hours":24}'

# add temporary rate-limit rule
curl -X POST -H "Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN_TOKEN" \
  https://gateway.redwood.internal/ratelimit/rules \
  -d '{"match":{"client_id":"svc-legacy-5"},"limit":10,"window_sec":60,"ttl_sec":900}'
```
ops-oncall: done — API returned 200. Added blocklist for the 3 most common IPs seen in the last 10m: 45.76.122.0/24, 185.230.60.0/24, 185.220.101.0/24. Throttle live in eu-west-1 and global fallback. Notifying support to expect helpdesk tickets.

alyssa: thanks. @devex please prep a short customer blurb so support can use consistent wording — we should avoid saying "breach" while we investigate.

devex: on it. Draft: "We're investigating an automated push notification surge that may cause repeated MFA prompts or temporary login difficulties for users. We're applying throttles and blocking malicious sources; if you see repeated prompts please escalate to support." Will post in >support-ready.

matt: quick forensic notes: checked KMS logs -> last API key rotation was 5d ago, no suspicious KMS access. Audit logs show a handful of failed SAML assertion attempts from rotating user agents. Saving full raw logs to s3://security-archive/2026/1728509999-authburst.log

kai: containment looks effective — push failure rates dropped ~85% in 12m after revokes+throttle. Users still reporting a few stray pushes but much lower. Next steps:
- complete full list of affected client_ids and tenants
- run credential leak checks for svc-legacy-5
- tune detection to avoid noisy revokes for service accounts
- draft post-incident runbook updates (MFA push backoff, client-level burst thresholds)

jess: also recommend: add a short cooldown on MFA prompt retries in SDK clients and doc the best-practice (exponential backoff). Ticketing: create follow-up in sec-ops backlog for RBAC audit and KMS permission review for service accounts.

ops-oncall: opened backlog items SECOPS-412 (RBAC audit), SECOPS-413 (KMS policy review), SECOPS-414 (detection tuning). Marking this thread as "contained" for now. Will keep monitoring 2h.

kai: nice work, team. We'll reconvene after the postmortem notes. :thumbsup:
